name: Monport GM 20W Fiber
tagline: Manual-focus integrated fiber for small tags: the entry model sold alongside the GM Pro
tldr: The GM 20W is the low-cost model on Monport's GM Pro page: an integrated 20W fiber with manual focus and a 110 × 110 mm field, $1,410 on Monport's store in October 2026. It suits tags, jewelry and small tools. Monport gives few figures for it: no source brand, depth or weight on the product page, so treat it as a budget marker rather than an engraving machine.
mainObjective: Low-cost marking of small metal parts

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $1,410 machine only, $1,560 with rotary axis, $1,610 with LightBurn Pro

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 110 × 110 mm field without repositioning

pros: Lowest price in Monport's fiber range at $1,410 (Monport store, Oct 2026)
Integrated one-piece design: source, galvo and column on a single base
Rotary and LightBurn bundles offered at the same small price steps as the Pro tiers
cons: Manual focus: height is set by hand for every new part
Small 110 × 110 mm field, limiting for tumblers and larger plates
Specs largely missing from the product page: source, marking depth and weight are not listed

faq.question: What does the GM 20W lack compared with the GM Pro tiers?
faq.answer: Autofocus and the electric lift: focus is set manually. The field is also smaller (110 × 110 mm instead of 150 × 150 mm), and Monport does not publish its source, depth or pulse figures in the comparison table that covers the Pro tiers.

faq.question: Can the GM 20W engrave deeply or cut metal?
faq.answer: It is not meant for that. A 20W Q-switched fiber marks and lightly engraves metal; deep relief and thin-sheet cut-outs take many passes and are better left to the higher-power tiers.

faq.question: Is the GM 20W worth it over a 20W integrated fiber from another brand?
faq.answer: It is priced in the same range as Gweike's G2 20W ($1,299) and close to the ComMarker B4 20W ($1,399). The GM 20W's case rests on Monport's US support and bundles; the published specs are thinner than its rivals', so compare field size and focus type before buying.

standoutFeatures.title: Monport's cheapest fiber
standoutFeatures.body: At $1,410 in October 2026, the GM 20W is the least expensive way into Monport's fiber range, with the same rotary and LightBurn bundle options as the Pro tiers.

standoutFeatures.title: Sized for small parts
standoutFeatures.body: The 110 × 110 mm field covers tags, rings, pendants, keys and small tools, the bread-and-butter of a home or market-stall marking business.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the manual-focus GM 20W sold on the GM Pro page. Compare the Pro tiers via the chips if you want autofocus or a larger field.
proTips: Use the red-dot preview and a focus gauge to set height precisely on each part type, then note the value for repeat jobs.

images.alt: Monport GM 20W manual-focus integrated fiber laser: Monport

editorialDepth.advantages: The GM 20W makes sense for a small marking side business on a strict budget: tags, jewelry and tools fit its field, and the price leaves room for an enclosure and safety gear.
editorialDepth.limitations: Manual focus slows mixed-height work, the field is small, and Monport publishes few specifications for this model. Anyone planning deep engraving should look at a higher-power tier.
